Within this framework, we propose a DM candidate consisting of a right-handed neutrino with a minimal mass threshold, allowing it to meet the observed DM abundance through its non-relativistic annulation processes. In addition, we examine constraints placed upon our model by direct detection experiments and cosmic background radiation, finding that it can satisfy these constraints with the Standard Model Higgs contributing minimally to its detection cross-section.

This study develops a point hypothesis filter for radar applications, featuring a discrete grid-based origin model and deriving an optimal solution through a data association approximation based on a scalar height function. A new height function is introduced, allowing existing implementation methods, and numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach under various levels of data association complexity. The developed framework offers flexibility for future sensor integration and resource allocation optimization. Existing methods either overlook complex data interactions or incur excessive computational costs, leaving a gap that this study aims to address, providing balanced performance in terms of accuracy, processing requirements, and generalizability.

This paper studies the null controllability in a population model that accounts for the impact of an interior decay source. By applying the method of moments and a uniqueness result with partial boundary observations and controls, we first establish an estimate for the controllable domain of the homogeneous system without control and boundary feedback, and then establish the null controllability of the controlled system and its connection to control time and domain, and the distributed control's ability to overcome interior decay when the control domain and control intensity are sufficiently large.

The dynamics of soccer games near the goal area demand swift decision-making by players, who must adapt to rapidly evolving situations to prevent goals and create scoring opportunities. This paper explores using enhanced actions in soccer games to improve the performance of a deep reinforcement learning model through a novel approach called FLEEL, a contact-aware variant of the last experience guided exploratory learning algorithm. By expanding the action space to include specific, temporary movements, our approach allows the agent to more effectively influence the game's outcome. We demonstrate the benefits of this approach by comparing it to a mainstream soccer simulation approach based on reinforcement learning and by showing how it can lead to more desirable results. Furthermore, we identify the next steps for further development of this methodology.

Time-domain extended source signal inversion has been previously analyzed in frequency domain studies. This research undertakes an numerical examination of domain time domain signal characteristics necessary for successful inversion. Our research undertakes an numerical examination of time-domain signal characteristics at various spatial locations in relation to the frequency domain equivalent. Results show that an reduction in bandwidth leads to significant delays in wave propagation, altering the apparent velocity. Our research also shows that an increase in source array extent results in decreased edge source signal quality, necessitating an analysis of time-domain extended source signal inverter capabilities. Our research also suggests that current signal inverter algorithms may produce erroneous results due to highly variable time-domain data characteristics.

We demonstrate the usage of squeezed vacuum to induce optical asymmetry in a two-level system, resulting in magnified differences in absorption and emission as the squeeze parameter increases. Our model utilizes the properties of the model to dissect the complex components of the density matrix, revealing that the asymmetry arises from the interplay between the Rabi frequency and the squeeze parameter. We also investigate how this optical asymmetry can be utilized to amplify the difference in population between the system's base states, potentially utilizing squeezed vacuum to achieve complete optical inversion through minimal external Rabi driving.

We have conducted in-depth analysis of X-ray data from high-state burst 2 of the black hole X-ray binary IGR J19294+1816 in 2019. Using X-ray data from NASA's AstroSat, we performed spectral and timing studies to understand the behavior of this source. Although the quality of the data is limited due to the presence of bursts, our findings suggest the existence of a high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillation at approximately 13.8 mHz. This is the highest recorded FHF-QPO for this class of binary systems. We have also identified a broad broad spectral feature in the 30-60 keN range, which is indicative of a cyclotron feature, centered around 45 keV with broad uncertainties. This is the second detection of a cyclotron feature in this binary system after its 2015 discovery. Furthermore, the observed parameters of the 2019 burst align with those of the 2015 burst and the giant bursts in 2001 and 2005. Consequently, we conclude that the physical mechanisms underlying the 2019 burst are the same as in previous high amplitude bursts of this binary system.

A noisy Ising version of a two-dimensional lattice model featuring nearest-neighbor competition and long-range migration on a two-dimensional grid is examined, focusing on the impact of noise on the coexistence of 'species' and the mechanism of species elimination through local interactions. By analyzing a phase diagram in relation to the strength of fluctuations and the intensity of the competition-colonization tradeoff, distinct regions of multi-species existence, a marginal region existence, and a region of binary coexistence are identified. Notably, an increase in fluctuations on the order of the critical exponent -3 in a 2D space prolongs the period of three-way coexistence but facilitates transitions to pairs coexistence, without affecting its fundamental shape. Simulations confirm these findings.

Ancient Sundials are revered historic timekeeping devices that demand careful preservation and study, given their declining usability in modern society. These analog devices, however, possess valuable scientific and artistic value, warranting preservation efforts. We have created a simple yet versatile database called Suryakala-Nusantara to digitally preserve and study Indonesian Sundials from various eras and regions. By assigning each timepiece a unique identifier, we can easily manage, edit, and analyze this collection of historic Sundials. The system's user-friendly web interface facilitates straightforward data editing and visualizations, including the creation of Google Maps and pie charts, through its integrated APIs. Furthermore, the platform enables cooperative research and preservation efforts among sundial enthusiasts and historians, allowing them to contribute to the preservation of these historic timepieces. The system's features, design, and potential advantages for studying Indonesian Ancient Sundials are also discussed.

This research explores the integration of cognitive reflecting surfaces (IRS) in 5G technology to improve energy efficiency in D2D communication. We analyze a scenario where an IRS-assisted D2D pair transmits data while an IRS-assisted cellular user sends data and power over the same frequency. By formulating an energy efficiency maximization problem, we consider D2D and cellular users adjusting their transmission powers and the IRS adjusting its virtual beamforming configuration. We solve this problem by creating a virtual beamforming design method and a user power optimization technique, and propose a joint optimization algorithm to maximize energy efficiency. Simulations show that our algorithm effectively balances energy efficiency and convergence speed by adjusting initial power values, and that fully connected IRS surfaces achieve higher energy efficiency than partially connected ones.

This paper presents a novel approach for obtaining two-dimensional distance readings from a single LDV at an remote location. Most existing methods only allow for one-dimensional measurements, which severely restricts data collection capabilities. By employing an arrangement of high-speed motors and rotating platforms, it is possible to determine an 2D position at a distant location using only a single LDV system. The proposed method involves an intricate mechanical design capable of generating an coordinate system that rotates around an origin point. This design allows for a variety of applications outside of land surveying, including but not limited to, topographical mapping and architectural planning.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates is being investigated 
for enhancing the coherence of transmission electron microscopy (TEM) sessions. 
Since their introduction to improve contrast in bright field imaging, researchers 
have explored diverse applications for these phase plates. While the potential 
to utilize the phase plate as an analytical tool has been demonstrated, its 
capability to compensate for spherical aberration in TEM imaging remains largely 
unexplored. This study delves into the potential of programmable phase plates to 
mitigate the negative impacts of lens spherical aberration in TEM imaging, by 
simulating the combined effects of the phase plate and the condenser lens on the 
image intensity. Although our simulations indicate that a programmable phase plate 
could in theory counterbalance the lens-induced distortions, the unpredictability 
of noise generated by the phase plate hinders its practical application for 
generating the desired point spread function. Furthermore, introducing the phase 
plate may introduce unintended consequences, potentially giving the illusion of 
higher resolution than actually exists. Ultimately, this investigation concludes 
that while the concept of utilizing a programmable phase plate to correct spherical 
aberration in TEM imaging is promising, there are several hurdles that need to be 
addressed before its practical implementation can be achieved.

The success of data-driven dialogue models heavily relies on input context, but it's challenging to accurately assess their encoder-generated representations due to the models' inherent randomness. These assessments are typically conducted in isolation from the model's generative process, which complicates comparing the complexity of the processed inputs to that of similar statistical structures. In this paper, we investigate whether the representations produced by generative dialogue models capture the necessary information for effective response generation. By leveraging recent advances in measuring symbolic and continuous representation complexity, we analyze the numerical representations generated by models like TAR and Transformer-TP, using tasks such as pseudo-Spanish Spanish and multiple multiple-choice dialogue tasks. Our experiments reveal significant variations in representation complexity across different tasks, correlated with generation difficulty, and sensitive to regularizations, suggesting that diagonalized penalty may guide the development of efficient representation learning algorithms. However, our analysis also exposes a shortcoming of current generative dialogue models in implicitly decoding causal relationships between conversations. To address this limitation, we propose a novel representation learning approach that explicitly encodes relational patterns, which outperforms the self-regulated methods in distribution measurement and model evaluation across all tested tasks. Deep learning methods have excelled in 2D LiDPlace data and image analysis, yet there's a lack of comprehensive research on using such techniques for 3D LiDPlace data. This study presents an innovative, attention-based deep learning network for LiDPlace recognition in three dimensions, featuring two novel architectures: a circular vector network that converts 3D LiDPointCloud data into angle-based feature vectors, and a linear network that processes the encoded features to create a place embedding. The attention mechanism allows the circular network to focus on LiDPointCloud elements vital for place identification. By leveraging the efficiency of attention and the speed of linear networks, our model achieves both high accuracy and speed in place recognition. The approach was tested on the Kitti dataset, and the results show the proposed network outperforms traditional methods like FARNet and HDNet in terms of accuracy, with a significant improvement of at least 15% better F-score than the baseline. Furthermore, our approach exhibits robustness against noise and speed, with a gain of at least 5% F-score compared to the standard linear network approach.

Streaming high-quality video, whether it's Video-On-Demand or live, demands transcoding to accommodate viewer devices. This requires significant computing power and, in many cases, cannot be live when utilizing legacy coders. Providing seamless access to video in real-time and real-quality thus necessitates the employment of multiple coding technologies, often heterogenous, across cloud platforms. Evaluating the performance of such setups is made difficult due to the lack of available data on coding speeds, which can vary depending on the type of code, input video properties, and available resources. In this paper, a transcoder with multiple codes is proposed and its performance can be modeled through the development of efficient import export technologies, presented and tested in this paper, leveraging the Google App Engine as an example cloud platform. The paper shows that the coding speeds can be modeled as exponential random variables and, in many cases, this approach can accurately predict the actual performance of the system, although it is observed that increasing the number of available coders may not always enhance system performance.

This study calculates the thermal screening properties of doped graphene at various temperatures, which is crucial for understanding and applying it in spintronic and magnetic applications. Our calculations determine the thermal capacity of doped graphene at different temperatures, utilizing a semi-classical model that considers velocity and density of states fluctuations. Our study reveals that thermal screening changes from v_F-fluctuation dominant at low temperatures to DOS-fluctuation dominant at high temperatures, with the transition dependent on doping level. Interestingly, the thermal capacity exhibits the characteristic peak associated with the van Hove singularity when there is sufficient DOS fluctuation.

Added mask-related information helped a model learn to connect speech sounds to their meaningful use, but it was unclear how effectively this approach could be applied when the speech was contextually relevant. To address this, we created MaskedSpeech, a comprehensive framework that includes a extensive dataset with coreferential three-way tree sentences and an associated audio recording. This framework evaluates the efficacy of masking strategies in speech production within a rich contextual framework. MaskedSpeech features a set of novel strategies for determining the degree to which the current linguistic form should be separated from its meaning. It was found that providing the model with the full meaning during the speech generation process, including the unrelated sentences, resulted in improved performance on the evaluation. We provide a detailed explanation of the linear and spectral stability properties of the solution to the Klein-Gordon equation with a discrete linear coupling and a single-degree-of-freedom anharmonic oscillator. Additionally, we have derived a crucial mathematical identity that enables the derivation of the required condition for the spectrum around the flat solution. Furthermore, we have obtained crucial bounds on the spectrum near two rotated solutions and established the sufficient condition for the orbital stability of these states.

Q-ball studies are expanded to include more complex field theories, potentially 
allowing for the discovery of quantum states within Q-balls. Under specific 
conditions, the profile of a multi-component field may show core structures,

We've re-examined the hypothesis of a holographic dark energy operating within a cyclic universe based on M-theory, considering its impact on the universe's fate. Initially, it was discovered that the size of the universe's cycles is dictated by the critical density at the end of the universe's life, influenced by the parameters of the holographic dark energy model. This has led some researchers to propose that these universe cycles would eventually accumulate, causing the universe to collapse. However, another group argued that the universe's expansion following each big bang would be sufficient to counterbalance this effect. To address this controversy, we performed a more in-depth analysis by calculating the universe's size at the beginning of each cycle using both approaches, which allowed us to determine that the universe would expand forever if there's a critical value for the universe's length.

Given a graph G and a Hermitian matrix A, we provide a formula for the scattering matrix S associated with the long-wavelength limit, based on the determinant-related expression. This formula can be used to derive further properties of S. Specifically, if A is a adjacency matrix of G, the magnitude of the element in row i and column j of S, denoted as S_{ij}, is found to be 2π times the sum of the squared coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of the subgraphs of G obtained by deleting the vertex v and adding two isolated vertices, where v is the k-th largest according to the pre-ordering generated by the squaring operation on subgraphs.

We examine Leopoldt-type theorems within non-commutative extensions of Q, specifically focusing on an infinite family of pairings between ideal classes in the integral integral group ring of the Q-extension A_n = C_{p^n}\times F_{p^n}. These branches belong to the family of p-Sylow subgroups of the integral integral group ring of F_{p^n}. We establish several types of equality and inequality relations for the I-rank and the v-determinant of the group ring B_n = Z[F_{p^n}], deriving consequences for the associated invariants of A_n, including the p-regulus. We prove theorems asserting the long-term average convergence of the p-regulus for each family, and investigate the p-class field theory implications, notably relating to Neukirch's conjecture. We establish the finite average limit of the p-regulus for three distinct theoretical frameworks, and derive a formula for the p-regulus expectation of the backward branching B_n within the context of Iwasawa theory.

This study examines the sensitivity of Belle II to allocate an allocation to a new type of particle, the axial vector meson, and investigate its connection to missing energy or photon interactions. By analyzing various decay processes involving B mesons and neutral kaons, we evaluate the ability of Belle II to detect these particles, including those that have not been previously studied in detail. Our analysis suggests that Belle II's extensive dataset can set stringent limits on the atomic vector meson's properties, potentially allocating it to a new type of particle with a higher degree of precision than current findings.

This research focuses on identifying changes in word meanings over time, a crucial aspect of semantic alteration detection. To tackle this issue, recent studies propose contextualized language models. However, despite their success in other tasks, these models have not been thoroughly examined in terms of their ability to detect shifts in meaning. Our analysis explores the problems associated with using contextualized language models for this purpose, including the reliance on surrounding text that may not be representative and their limited ability to capture nuances of word meanings. Our findings suggest that contextualized language models are not well-suited for detecting changes in meaning, leading us to suggest an alternative approach that outperforms the current methods.

The evolution of radio galaxies and heavy quasars is heavily influenced by accretion disks that can be overwhelmed by the potential emission of ultralight bosons through the spin-down of the black hole's mass. This work compares the theoretical emission rates of these ultralight bosons to the observed properties of 11 radio galaxies and heavy quasars, characterized by their masses, ages, and emission at a 5.8 GHz frequency. Our analysis suggests that ultralight bosons emitted from the black holes of these objects are generally insufficient to account for the observed emission, although there is a notable discrepancy between observed and predicted emission rates in the mass range of $10^{-12}$ to $10^{-10}$ $M_{\odot}$. This discrepancy arises from an observed emission that exceeds current theoretical models by several orders of magnitude.

Investigating vertebrate neuroepithelial cells' interkinetic nuclear migration in relation to zebrafish retinal proliferation has been the subject of multiple studies. A significant observation made across these studies is that approximately 75% of these cells undergo nuclear migration from the basal to the apical region during a specific time frame. This study focuses on analyzing retinal movie data in a non-invasive and statistically robust manner. A novel approach is proposed for estimating the movement velocities of chromatin threads and for estimating state transition probabilities. A statistical assessment further validates the results obtained with this approach. Our ultimate goal is to returally model the typical behavior of these cells. Our findings suggest that during G1 phase, the nuclear position is maintained, and during S phase, there is a high probability of transitioning to an S-state from any G1-state. Our model classifies M1 as part of the S1 state and suggests that an post-M state in combination with nuclear positioning could describe the same condition. A key conclusion suggested here is that during retinal development, C. hausseri, there may not be distinct phases for retinal cell cycles, and rather, there could be specific conditions that define different 'states'.

In various low-level image and video tasks using color images, such as video completion and color image demosaicing, real-world data often lacks synchronization across color channels and results in a highly underdetermined system. Until now, the statistical independence of negative binomial distributions has been leveraged to model such data, thanks to their success in color image reconstruction from incomplete pixel samples. However, applying this technique to temporal color video reconstruction has been hindered by the computational intensity of co-occurrence modeling. To address this, the proposed code-based negative binomial distribution (CBNB) introduces an alternative code to enhance the coherence of the temporal model, thus capturing temporal color video relationships more effectively and enabling a sparse representation under Fourier transformation. The proposed code-based approach can be interpreted as a refined unsharp masking operation, incorporating both convolution and differential operations. To tackle the highly underdetermined nature of the problem, a code-sinc coherent patch algorithm (CCPA) is devised, incorporating a coherent patch update rule and an adaptive code update rule (CACUR) within an iterative proximal gradient (IPG) framework. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed CCBN and CCPA's superiority over the code-based synthetic Nesterov's algorithm (BSNA) and other comparative methods in color video reconstruction tasks. Furthermore, to address the high computational cost of the coherent patch update rule, a fast coherent update rule (FCUR) is introduced and integrated into an iterative multi-proximal gradient (IMPG)

We've developed a new theoretical model to analyze the dynamics of polar active fluids that have been contained within a fixed area and have experienced random disturbances in two- or three-dimensional spaces. Unlike previous models that focused on two-dimensional scenarios and yielded unstable systems due to symmetry-breaking, our theory provides insights into the effects of disorder in higher-dimensional spaces, specifically three-dimensional spaces. Our findings suggest that in environments with dimensions greater than two, disordered systems can exhibit localized states, influenced by the system's geometry and the nature of the disturbances. These states can be unstable, displaying chaotic behavior, or stable, exhibiting long-term predictable patterns. In today's highly interconnected world, understanding the risks associated with complex networks is becoming increasingly vital. In this study, we examine a well-known measure of node significance called betweenness and explore its potential flaws in the context of scientific collaboration networks. Our analysis is conducted on three distinct networks, representing different time periods from 1994-1998 to 2004-2008, and we become concerned to discover that betweenness often underrates the importance of new key nodes emerging within the network. Furthermore, our research reveals a misleading correlation that appears to suggest the vulnerable nodes with high betweenness values are well-established established nodes with long-standing research histories. Ultimately, our findings suggest that betweenness can provide only a rough guideline for potential network attacks or failures, and we emphasize the importance of considering network dynamics when seeking to protect complex interconnected systems.

Investigating high-angle photoemission spectra of La$_{2}$CuO$_{4}$ enables the examination of its pseudogapped region above the Fermi level. The study reveals that the anomalously rapid energy evolution of these pseudogaps near the zone boundary is influenced by electron-electron interactions that vary across space. Many-body calculations utilizing a Hubbard model demonstrate that this reduction in variability arises from the competition between short-range and long-range order mechanisms. Specifically, the study shows that a separation of charges within a rectangular lattice configuration effectively strong correlates with a reticular pattern and maintains the distinct behavior of the pseudogaps observed in photoemission spectra. Furthermore, investigating a strongly correlated, single-site system and discovering its highly charged states limitations motivate the exploration of an alternative strong correlation – magnetic order. It is these two systems bordering on metallic behavior, exhibiting magnetic or charge order, as their critical points, where the distinct evolution of the pseudogaps is located. Near these two critical points, the distinct movement of the pseudogap's edge occurs, yet it displays significantly limited movement between these two critical points.

This letter describes a specialized apparatus designed to study the effects of spallation neutrons at the Aberdeen Tunnel laboratory in Inverness. The device utilizes a conventional 35 MeV proton beam and incorporates a specialized chamber made of steel, which increases the impact of the beam, allowing for the extraction of a more intense neutron flux. By maximizing the energy carried by the spallation neutrons, the device can effectively replace a higher energy proton beam in certain types of nuclear research. Furthermore, the device has been upgraded to its current form, described in this letter, after initially being built to its basic form in 1997 and subsequently upgraded to its present state in 2007.

The growth of the Indonesian internet user population has necessitated a nomenclature that enables a seamless exchange of information between individuals. To facilitate this, identifying and extracting vital details from Indonesian citizens, such as their names, dates of birth, gender, issuing authority, expiration date, citizen identification numbers, and gender can be achieved through ID card extraction using optical character recognition and natural language processing. The proposed method employs Python programming, the OpenCV library for ID card detection, the Tesseract library for ID card text extraction, and the NLTK package for text cleaning and data processing. When put into practice, this method demonstrated a level of accuracy of 71.43%, indicating its effectiveness and efficiency. Moreover, it offers a user-friendly and user-centric experience, providing users with secure and reliable access to information they are seeking.

A simulation system was set up to accurately compute the probability distribution of a quantum harmonic oscillator in its ground state, both without and with consideration of a drive force. Computational experiments demonstrated high accuracy, with relative errors around $10^{-4}$ when comparing theoretical and simulated results for various scenarios including different frequencies, drive strengths, and times. Notably, the simulation consistently achieved this level of accuracy regardless of the system parameters.

By analyzing new light curve data and incorporating previously published observations, the researchers determined the rotation characteristics of three asteroids: 10115 1992 SK, 1685 Toro, and 1620 Geographos. Geographos was found to have multiple spin periods, while the others do not show this pattern. Notably, the study provides the first evidence of the YORP effect on Geographos's rotation acceleration. The measured acceleration values for all asteroids fall within the predicted theoretical range of accelerations caused by the YORP effect, based on various models and assumptions regarding their surface properties and shapes. Geographos is considered the most suitable target for future studies of the YORP effect's impact on the rotation acceleration of small, highly inactive asteroids. A table comparing the estimated acceleration on Geographos with theoretical predictions is also presented in the study.

The youth are increasingly shaping political discussions on social media platforms, making them crucial for understanding the political landscape of the future. We have collected an original dataset from the Instagram accounts of major Italian politicians and their fans, creating an information flow graph that maps out political dialogues. By analyzing this graph, we have identified community structures within the information network and explored how it evolves over time, as well as the diverse sources of new information that feed into the network. We have also investigated the technological underpinnings, linguistic styles, and generical classifications of posts that drive the dynamics of the political conversations.

We show that collections of homeomorphisms of a topological surface that preserve a set of disjoint simple closed curves and act minimally on the space obtained by cutting the surface along these curves and closing the boundaries are both locally compact and have a topology of convergence that makes them a uniformality space. Additionally, we prove that collections of surface homeomorphisms that preserve these closed curves and act mildly locally with respect to some topology are non-metrizable in the topology of convergence but can be embedded into the general linear group of a vector space. This implies that the general linear group topology converges to a surface homeomorphism collection is strictly weaker than the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Furthermore, collections of surface homeomorphisms that preserve these closed curves and act minimally on the space obtaining by filling the components between the curves with convex hulls are not topologically equivalent. This shows that the collection of anti-diffeomorphisms of the disc is not homeomorphic to the collection of homeomorphisms of the disc.

We analyzed 147 M-dwarfs with extensive spectroscopic and photometric data, including near-infrared spectra, to evaluate various stellar parameter estimation methods. 
We tested the reliability of existing stellar parameter estimators and explored potential improvements for more accurate results.

We found that all these approaches yielded comparable outcomes, but we improved results by separating the sample into subsets with consistent spectral types, reducing results by a factor of nearly 1.5. 
We also found that utilizing different estimators did not significantly improve the final results, suggesting that a traditional code may perform as well as advanced machine learning techniques. 
We assessed the precision of the derived results and found that all methods yielded similar accuracy. 
We also evaluated the impact of metal abundance (Fe/H) on the determined stellar parameters, finding that all the tested methods were largely insensitive to this factor. 
We also tested the performance of these methods on a well-characterized field sample and a binary star sample with reliably measured stellar parameters.

In the study of ripple transport on a line ripple, we investigate how to steer the ripple in a dual metasurface by modifying the grain's linear momentum. A theoretical model is developed to control the transport of optical ripples and demonstrate line ripple's unique properties, which could be utilized for ratchet applications. Specifically, we show that line ripple can be fully stopped, fully transported in the opposite direction, or trapped within the grid when exposed to a dual metasurface. By using a textured grain and an elliptical wave, we achieve partial line ripple transport in the opposite direction. The ability to stop or transport line ripple in a dual metasurface can be efficiently realized with minimal wave complexity.

Although it's well-known that determining 5-WCC in acyclic queries without direct edges is solvable in polynomial time, no corresponding result exists for its counterpart with self-joins. This paper addresses this gap in research. We first show that Direct Acyclic Queries (DAQs) with self-joins are precisely equivalent to 3-WCC in the context of tuple self-references. Furthermore, we discover that DAQs with self-joins can have different complexity classifications, including coNP-completeness, 3-WCC-hardness, and 5-WCC hardness. Notably, we provide a new, simpler proof for a recently found family of DAQs with self-joins that are both 5-WCC-complete and self-referential.

The concept of regular methods gained popularity due to its effectiveness in solving word and tree problems within first-order logic and its connection to Satisfiability Modulo Theories. Although existing work on infinite words focuses on ordinary trees and has produced regular method equivalents like ω-RMTs and regular simulations, most approaches are existential and therefore unable to directly support model expansion. This work presents a new synthesis of computable regular methods for infinite words, utilizing a fresh perspective from finite indexability. Our approach unifies previous results and can be extended to trees. Furthermore, we establish a direct link between ω-RMTs and regular simulations on infinite words and derive an effective transformation from one to the other.

This report presents  measurements  of the branching fractions for $B^+ \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ and provides estimates for the branching fractions of $B^0 \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ and $B^0 \to K^{*0} K^{*0}$ decays. The study of these processes is conducted using data from the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 3.0 fb^-1 and 5.3 fb^-1 at charm-threshold energy points.

Recent advances in machine learning and optimization have led to the development of symbolic regression techniques that enable the reconstruction of equations by analyzing measured data. Building on this research, this work presents a method for identifying unobserved dynamic behaviors in a system from measured data. This technique first uses a machine learning approach to expand the dynamically relevant part of a transfer function, and then employs an optimization algorithm to refine it. The resulting model can simulate the dynamics and predict dynamic behaviors that were not present in the measured data. Using the chaotic Lozi map as an example, various dynamic regimes are first encoded into attractor shapes and then transmitted over a channel. The proposed method successfully recovers the transmitter's Lozi dynamics and reveals that the unseen attractor shapes are indeed present when new inputs are applied.

This study develops an unbiased estimator for the mean absolute deviation of a median-based distribution, utilizing independent and identically distributed random variables taking values in a non-randomized form. A associated regression-based estimator for the asymptotic variance is introduced, which demonstrates improved accuracy in variance estimation through numerical experiments compared to existing methods. Furthermore, the use of a bootstrap procedure to approximate variance yields accurate confidence intervals, as demonstrated in a real-data example.

To prevent a differential game from reaching a specific target, an controller aims to make a player as ineffective as possible by optimally controlling the target's state. We examine the single-player variant of this game, focusing on its ability to reach a given set of states within a set time frame, under the optimal control of the controller. A Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation describes the states where the player can successfully reach the target set by the end of the designated time period, when controls are applied optimally. We establish that there exists an optimal control that enables the player to achieve the greatest effectiveness, resulting in the states where the target set is optimally reached, by the time period in question. This state corresponds to the set of states where the player can successfully reach the given set by applying the optimal control, limited by the time period. A quadratic approximation of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation is proposed to calculate the reachable set at an earlier time, based on the reachable sets at two later times. This approach provides an efficient method for estimating the reachable set at an earlier time, given the reachable sets at two later times.

To effectively train deep neural networks, particularly during the tuning of hyperparameters, logging and visualization play crucial roles. However, current methods suffer from limitations in compatibility with various models and training frameworks, often failing to accommodate complex operations like those found in neural networks. This paper introduces an innovative approach to log and visualize training data as a function of location within a model. Our method, LAFL, utilizes a periodic, fluctuating activation strategy to automatically generate an attention mechanism that highlights significant operations. By allocating specific logging tasks to these high attention operations, we can extract representative samples that illustrate the training data. Experimental results across multiple classification and regression models demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in producing accurate and generalizable visualizations.

The precise structure of the ventral temporal cortex remains a topic of debate, with research suggesting that the animacy distinction may be centrally located within this region. Our study employs a unique approach, using a comprehensive set of 333 natural objects to reveal a highly interconnected network in the ventral temporal cortex. Our results indicate that this core network has a distinct preference for animal objects, while surrounding areas show more varied patterns. These findings, which align with both previous research and recent neural processing models, suggest that the animacy distinction arises from the contrasting patterns of connectivity and activation across the temporal lobe.

This research paper proves the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture for a substantial subset of the GL(2) space, specifically related to the rate at which certain mathematical forms converge, which in turn provides a stronger support for the Landau-Siegel zeros conjecture. Our proof builds upon a framework by Bhargava and Shah and utilizes the method of test functions to analyze the distribution of zeros in these mathematical forms. Ultimately, our findings expand the previously known results by a significant factor of 10^3 in terms of the magnitude of the parameter 't'.

Dennis Diaconescu built the quantum relational hoare logic framework to extend the quantum sequential operational framework, making it possible to analyze programs using Hoare logic and support for concurrency via logic implications. Building on this foundation, we expand the framework by integrating expectations and the ability to reason about expectations under concurrency. These additions enable the investigation of quantum expectations as invariants and co-invariants, and ultimately as assertions in the sense of Reynolds. By extending the language to include expectations, we demonstrate preservation of equivalence and valid distributed programming practices using quantum relational hoare logic with expectations.

The COVID-19 pandemic in Italy, particularly in Lombardy, has been characterized by a single large spreading event that may have accelerated its progression. This observation raises questions about the role of super-spreader events in the dynamics of all diseases transmitted aerosol. This research aims to explore this issue by examining network models that transmit infection, focusing on how a significant, highly contagious event influences the rate at which infections spread, rather than just examining degree distributions. Two simple models were used to investigate this problem: an event-driven version of the configuration model, in infection-inducing networks, in comparison to its version as a random graph. Findings revealed that incorporating a large spreading event in any of these models accelerates the infection's transmission, regardless of the underlying network structure. Moreover, in models that require close contact, a significant spreading event has analogous effects to increasing the average network connectivity. In contrast, in models transmissible via air, it resembles a dramatic influx of new nodes into the network. This research suggests that air-borne infections should be analyzed by taking into consideration highly contagious spikes in any large data sets.

Let T be a collection of continuous linear operators acting on a complex, topological vector space V. This collection T is said to be cyclic if there's a specific vector u within V for which the set of vectors obtained by applying all possible combinations of T to u is dense in V. This paper delves into the properties and applications of compact, cyclic sets of operators under the assumption that they consist of operators that commute with one another. Additionally, the concept of locally cyclic sets of operators is introduced and explored.

The paper discusses the difficulty in accurately measuring solar vector magnetic fields due to the absence of direct measurement techniques. This leads to the rapid adoption of inference-based methods, which use intensity and polarization data from photometric spectrospectrometers to magnetic field calculations based on radiative transfer and inversion theories. A crucial assumption in these calculations is that the solar atmosphere behaves like a radiative equilibrium, and the accuracy of this assumption can be compromised by instrumental bias in the acquisition of intensity and polarization data. Although previous studies have identified the negative impact of such bias on magnetic field inference, there is a lack of investigation into its origin. In this study, we examine various forms of bias, including static, time-series, and gradient-related biases, and determine their impact on cross-correlation and phase shift between the Loewen and Stenflo diagrams. We then assess how these biases affect magnetic field inference under both relaxed and strict strong test field assumptions, using a non-linear inversion code (NRSEL). In this process, we also collect and visualize a large dataset (over 170 TB) of reduced Inverse Free data to investigate potential causes of such bias, including differences in the cross-correlation between spectrographs and effects of polarization calibration. As a result, we identify specific strategies to alleviate such bias, including the use of customized comparison files, the selection of specific spectral lines, and the alignment of polarization calibration grids.

A comprehensive analysis has been conducted to determine the physical extent of 79 young stellar clusters in nine diverse galaxies. Using observational data from various studies, the authors measure the radii of these clusters and develop an empirical formula for predicting their size. The results show that the radii of these stellar clusters range from as small as 2.4 parsecs to as large as 110.0 parsecs. The measured values are comparable to those of supershells within the Milky Way when analyzing small to medium-sized stellar clusters. The authors' analysis also reveals that the dynamic state of the host galaxy does not significantly impact the size of the stellar clusters. The authors' study further defines the typical size of young stellar clusters in various galaxies as between 30 to 50 parsecs, which may have a universal significance. The authors' analysis is a crucial step in understanding how giant molecular clouds are mixed and how they influence the distribution of ionizing radiation and stellar winds. The authors' findings may also have a crucial role in shaping the evolution of star formation within galaxies. The authors' analysis is further relevant to similar studies conducted within the Milky Way and how they may have a crucial role in understanding the mixing of molecular gas and the redistribution of radiation and stellar winds in galaxy disks.

We present a novel, unorthodox method to calculate the decay width of hadrons decaying into two photons, specifically by correlating lepton currents at distinct points in spacetime. This approach is conceptually straightforward yet encounters challenges related to the ambiguity of hadron states when correlations are applied too early. We've successfully applied this method to lattice calculations of $\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma$, demonstrating its validity. The event's morphology and necessary distortions to obtain the correlation between hadron states and momenta are investigated. Moreover, we present an alternative strategy utilizing effective field theory to eliminate unnecessary calculations, thereby enhancing statistical accuracy. This alternative is also implemented and compared with the primary method.

A major obstacle in modeling solids with interacting electrons through quantum Monte Carlo is the Hubbard sign problem, which drastically increases computational costs at high doping levels. This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture that utilizes complex-valued networks and generates flexible, non-gauge-style current configurations. The proposed model demonstrates significantly improved efficiency, exhibiting up to an eightfold reduction in statistical variance and a corresponding decrease in required computational samples compared to traditional methods.

Shannon previously explored the concept of $N$-integers, which are numbers less than or equal to a given positive integer $N$ that can be formed by multiplying two distinct prime numbers. She investigated the count of these $N$-integers and its relation to the prime numbers $N$ can be formed by. In this paper, we focus on a specific subset of $N$-integers, which cannot be formed by multiplying three distinct prime numbers. We examine the behavior of this subset's count, particularly in relation to the Dickman $\rho$ function, which has been recently re-introduced by Alon and Friedgut. We derive an updated formula for the count of this specific $N-integer$ subset and derive an upper limit for the Dickman-related parameter. Furthermore, we discuss potential methods to enhance this upper limit and provide numerical evidence to support our claims.

Given any non-erasing free monoid homomorphism σ and subshift X that has high topological entropy, we find a closed subset X' within X that behaves like the σ-image of X. This subset X' maintains the same language and entropy as X, yet may have lower complexity. If the entropy of X is zero, the ratio of complexity to language at n grows no faster than n to the power of (t/T)(1+o(1)) as n approaches infinity, where T represents the shortest length of a word in X generated by applying σ repeatedly to any element of the free basis of X. Specifically, if the entropy of X is positive, there's a uniform bound (2t+1)(t+1)+1 for the sum of complexities divided by the sum of entropies of subshifts obtained by applying σ^k to X for all non-negative integers k. By leveraging previously learned skills, multitasking can be accelerated and streamlined.  Typically, a single model is trained to tackle multiple tasks, but in this paper, we explore an alternative approach: cross-task generation.  We seek to achieve on new tasks by leveraging models trained on unrelated tasks.  Unlike conventional methods, we do not anticipate the new tasks.  Equipped with only input examples and no corresponding labels, we aim to generate corresponding output labels.  To obtain this, we employ an unsupervised approach for hierarchical clustering and define task-specific labels as unique task names.  We enhance the retrieval component to obtain relevant hidden representations from the model based on input examples and utilize a diverse and rich "knowledge library" composed of all trained tasks.  We demonstrate our method on distinct task settings, including sentiment analysis and part-of-speech tagging.  Our results indicate that the proposed method surpasses unsupervised counterparts and performs comparable to supervised methods in certain settings.

This paper introduces the M-fast Autonomous Component Analysis (M-ar-K-Fast), a rapid method for detecting changes in the overall structure of high-dimensional data. Initially, we outline the principles of the Markov Random Field (MRF) model, a type of probabilistic graph, before demonstrating how it can be used to model data structure. Subsequently, we explain the Fast Independent Component Analysis (FICA) algorithm, an efficient variant of the standard ICA, designed for real-time processing. By combining the MRF and FICA principles, the M-ar-K-Fast algorithm is proposed, allowing for real-time monitoring of high-dimensional data. This method offers the advantages of both the MRF and FICA, including the ability to process a continuous data stream. The M-ar-K-Fast is applied in the context of machinery fault diagnosis, specifically for identifying novel faults. Furthermore, we integrate the Kullback-Leibler divergence and the maximum a posteriori estimation to evaluate the postulated data structure and eliminate spurious components that may arise during the detection of new faults. The M-ar-K-Fast outperforms the current methods in accuracy and efficiency, as verified by our experiments.

The gaming sector, though heavily focused on software quality and user experience, lacks thorough examination of requirements engineering practices. To address this gap, a comprehensive survey was conducted to investigate the current state of requirements engineering in the gaming industry and gather information to develop a framework for practitioners and researchers. The survey's results reveal several key characteristics of the gaming industry and reveal several areas of ambiguity. Notably, there is significant emphasis on user feedback and testing, as well as iterative development, to minimize risks associated with investment. The survey's findings can be utilized to investigate specific requirements engineering aspects, such as representation, management, validation, and collaboration. The survey's contribution lies in its detailed description of the current state of requirements engineering in the gaming industry, as well as its detailed data, which can be utilized to develop a framework for practitioners and researchers in the industry.

The achievement of high performance in private machine learning models relies heavily on carefully selecting hyperparameters, particularly the degree of privacy loss. However, optimal hyperparameter selection in private models cannot be accomplished through standard, unprivate methods due to information constraints imposed by differential privacy. Consequently, a new, privacy-aware hyperparameter optimization approach is essential to enable the full potential of private models. In this research, we focus on optimizing two critical hyperparameters in the K-nearest neighbors classifier: the number of neighbors and the distance threshold for neighbor selection. By incorporating the hyperparameters into the private multi-class classification framework, we develop an optimization method that balances model performance with the cost of privacy loss incurred during prediction. This approach yields a new, privacy-aware utility function tailored to evaluating model performance, which guides our proposed optimization strategy. The outcome is a novel, adaptable hyperparameter optimization method applicable to a range of private algorithms and hyperparameters. When applied to the private KNN classifier, this method outperforms traditional, unprivate optimization techniques and yields a fully private model with superior performance in comparison to models trained with optimally selected hyperparameters.
A strategy is outlined for analyzing boolean subalgebras of the algebra of all involutions on a given set, with specific research results addressing algebras defined by certain operation symbols.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence nearly all astronomical research areas by carrying the EUI NISP instrument which comprises the VIS and NIR VIS subsystems. The EUI NISP's three-channel detectors experience correlated noise due to their shared pixel readout, which could impact the measurement of the spectral energy distribution and the cosmological parameters LEAR will explore the effect of correlated readout noise on the accuracy of spectral measurements and the efficacy of nulling experiments using the EUI NISP's NIR spectrograph and the MSU, anticipating the significance of this effect after considering the cosmic variance during the EUI NISP's 10-year mission. Our findings show that correlated readout noise could impact the measurement of the spectral slope and the efficacy of the MSU for cosmological parameter estimation by a significant margin, underscoring the importance of accurately modeling correlated noise in future analyses and the necessity of calibrating this effect using the MSU.

We applied two distinct chemical classification models to a large dataset of 72000 stars from the APOGEE-DR16, using a chemical cartography approach. The first model was a standard approach using 16 main abundances, while the second used 34 features derived from machine learning through drift estimation. The second model's performance was evaluated by comparing the rate of misclassified stars to the first model's results using a method called the delta test. The second model showed significant improvements of 10-30% in results for certain star populations in the Milky Way's disk. The APOGEE-DR16's rich dataset allowed for a more comprehensive analysis of galaxy cartography, using 34 chemical features instead of the usual 16. The cartography was created by establishing relationships between 128% of the stars and fitting a non-linear model to the data. The results were further validated by calculating the residual abundances for each star, essentially measuring the distance from a star to its closest match, and comparing the outcomes to the first model's results. The cartography approach using 34 chemical features provided more accurate results in the main population band, mainly due to a more precise classification of low-metallicity stars. While it did not significantly improve results for intermediate populations due to broader dispersion, the cartography method did lead to more precise results for thick and thin disks, likely due to better classification of low-metallicity stars

During the COVID-19 pandemic in China, a significant number of rumors disseminated via the internet posed both psychological and physical threats to society, hindering the combined efforts of governments and the public to manage the pandemic. To effectively measure the influence of these rumors and identify the key individuals responsible for their dissemination, this study proposes an enhanced model based on the Spread Method (SSM-GA). By integrating the principles of information flow and removing unnecessary constraints, this improved model more accurately captures the progression of online rumors. Experiments conducted on three typical rumor types - those related to vaccines, protective equipment, and the pandemic itself - demonstrate the suitability and superiority of the SSM-GA model in evaluating the influence of these rumors and pinpointing the most influential accounts responsible for their rapid dissemination. Moreover, the SSM-GA model can be applied to monitor real-time information propagation during the pandemic, providing a valuable reference for designing effective anti-rumor strategies.

A rare and luminous type of extragalactic objects, planetary nebulae can be used as standard candles to measure distances. By analyzing a sample of over 1100 planetary nebulae in 27 objects within the Fornax cluster, we established the first independent distances to nine galaxies. The data for this analysis was adapted from the ONC3D and local planetary nebulae data sets. Using the ratio of core to halo densities in the PBPH method, we determined relative distances between the measured objects and the Scylla galaxy in the Fornax cluster. The results of this study were correlated with existing data from the SNOS, ONC3D, and SDSS projects, confirming a strong relationship between planetary nebulae diaphragms and galaxy morphological types. Ultimately, our analysis enabled the accurate measurement of relative distances for 8 out of the 9 measured objects, with the most notable examples being the Triangulum III, Carina's Shell, and the Triangulum II galaxies. The data for this analysis was made available on the ONC3D website.

Every minute, the Instagram feed is updated with new posts for every user, providing a continuously advancing list. This concept, known as a periodic stream, refers to real-world services like Twitter's timeline and Instagram feed that update in batches at set intervals. Periodic streams are ubiquitous in both public and enterprise APIs.

However, there are significant performance and reliability shortcomings associated with periodic streams. Many servers simply crash under the immense load, often exceeding their capacity to handle them efficiently. To effectively manage periodic streams, they must be processed alongside irregular data at both high speeds and low volumes.

Introducing a new type of high-performance flow processing engine, designed specifically to tackle periodic streams. This innovative solution is named after the continuous flow of data it can handle, akin to a rushing stream. It is currently being utilized in production environments by small to mid-sized companies, including those in the fashion, marketing, and advertising industries, as well as in the gaming sector, primarily in the form of an Instagram feed reader that's been optimized to utilize multiple cores for maximum efficiency, preventing server crashes under heavy load. This system's architecture is now being further developed to provide a more thorough performance analysis, along with related benchmarks, to better understand its potential in a wider range of periodic stream scenarios, including those found at both small and large scale operations, including those utilized by leading tech giants, such as Google, Facebook, and Alibaba, which also rely on periodic streams in both their public and private services, such as

This research paper confirms that both Bertrand curves when associated with a timelike curve and a timelike Bertrand curve pair cannot exist within a certain type of space. It also determines the specific conditions for a spacelike curve to have a certain property and identifies a specific type of timelike curve that is defined by two specific functions.

The choice of loss function for a classification model is commonly considered essential, yet the design of the ideal loss function for a given task remains largely unexplored. This study investigates how the ideal loss function may vary depending on factors outside the model, such as the input data and the architecture employed, for a set of straightforward neural network classification tasks. Two key questions guide this research: (a) the degree of model robustness to the loss function, and (b) the indicator of an optimal loss function category. Our analysis indicates that the level of model robustness to the loss function is influenced by the underlying task and is closely tied to the concept of mutual information. Moreover, information-theoretic properties help define an ideal loss function and provide a practical solution to it.

This paper explores the stabilization of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in a domain using a boundary feedback controller applied to a tilted side boundary. We prove that a linear feedback controller can achieve asymptotic stability for well-mixed (homogeneous) boundary conditions, and nonlinear feedback controllers can achieve exponential stability under both well-posed boundary conditions. Additionally, our results hold true for non-sticky (slip) boundary conditions.

This research develops a computational framework for modeling crystallization
processes driven by mechanical stress and temperature differences. The proposed
approach is integrated into a microstructurally informed simulation system, which
takes into account the changes in phase boundary due to thermal expansion and
yield stress, as well as the influence of pressure and strain rate on material
properties using the Barlett equation of state, Arrhenius law, and the Von Mises
yield criterion. A high-level language called C++ is employed to create an adaptive
finite element model, which utilizes the Method of Modified Lines (MMAC) to solve
the coupled system of balance equations and a kinetic model based on the Cox-Merz
rule. The computational framework is verified using a simplified scenario
involving the crystallization of liquid sulfur and later demonstrated with a more
complex material, PEEK, which exhibits significant structural changes upon
processing. The results obtained with the developed code accurately replicate
experimental observations, revealing distinct mechanical wave patterns and
temperature distributions within the material sample.

To analyze the impact of external magnetization on spin-triplet Cooper pairs in nematic superconductors, we calculated the Pauli susceptibility using a neutron-proton mixture as a model system. By applying the BCS approximation, we found the susceptibility's dependence on the attractive interaction and external field, taking into account the anisotropy of the superconducting state. Our results demonstrated that the linear response to an external field varies based on the d-wave symmetry of the superconducting pair, and the calculated phase diagram illustrates the impact of an external field on different d-wave states.

External predictors, such as those providing end-effector position and force information, are highly effective in guiding learning robots to execute tasks. This is because they capture the global consequences of actions and consequently, loss functions derived from these controllers can be quite misleading. To prevent the robot from learning suboptimal actions, we propose developing a controller that utilizes feedback that reflects actions with the same cost as the optimal action. Unfortunately, directly obtaining such feedback is not feasible. In this research, we present an algorithm that applies a statistical transformation to data from external teachers that is guaranteed to preserve the optimal action's probability distribution under certain conditions. This is illustrated by applying the algorithm to offline and online learning scenarios using a robotic arm.

The typical differential continuous phase modulation (CPM) detection process involves a memory of $L$ symbols, which can be reduced to $L/2$ symbols for certain CPM schemes, such as Gaussian CPM with a linear pulse shape. The requirement for differential detection to maintain the same CPM differential signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) degradation can involve an even larger memory of symbols. In this work, we introduce an innovative differential detection method for CPM that utilizes a shorter memory matrix to achieve the same SNR performance as the conventional non-coherent detection method at the given SNR level. The proposed method reduces the required memory to a significantly smaller length, specifically $1/L$ symbols. We provide theoretical analysis and numerical results to demonstrate the proposed method's effectiveness, notably in the high-SNR environment. Notably, the need for differential detection to maintain the same CPM differential SNR performance can be reduced to an even smaller memory of approximately $1/L$ symbols, specifically in the high-SNR environment. We outperform the conventional differential detection method by a substantial margin in terms of the required memory length, specifically in the high-SNR environment.

The detection of merged neutron star-black holes by gravitational-wave interferometers raises questions about how the neutron star's mass loss during a core-collapse supernova affects this process. Comparing this mass with that expelled during supernovae on white-dwarf surfaces reveals the necessity of detailed simulations considering core-collapse dynamics. Nonetheless, the potential for such mergers to produce electromagnetic counterparts remains largely unexplored. It is hypothesized that the intense X-rays and radio bursts from the black-hole merger could be significantly hindered by the material shed during the supernova, thereby limiting their detectability. Conversely, visible light signals from the neutron star could still be detected despite the mass loss, provided the material shed during the supernova isn't too dense. These findings highlight the potential for future interferometers to drastically enhance the accuracy of estimating supernovae outcomes on white-dwarf surfaces.

A previously reported finding indicates that the relativistic quantum field theory (RQFT) vacuum experiences changes in compliance as temperature rises above the absolute zero point, resulting in a decrease in density and an increased compressibility. We have previously shown that this discovery leads to the exclusion of the Minkowski vacuum in RQFT as a reliable model for spacetime. In the current paper, the investigation of compressibility in various spacetimes has been expanded to include asymptotically flat spacetimes. The primary approach involves analyzing the RQFT vacuum in de Sitter space, the AdS cavity, and the exterior Schwarzschild spacetimes. The discovery that some complex spacetimes exhibit compressibility matching that of the RQFT states suggests that these models maintain their relevance. In contrast, the compressibility behavior in some simpler spacetimes has been found to be anomalous.

Heavy rainfall severely disrupts outdoor activities and infrastructure, posing significant safety concerns and economic challenges in developed areas. Despite these issues, current approaches to predicting rain affected regions often fail due to the lack of actual rain information in input data. This study presents a novel, bidirectional system that can simultaneously create and remove rain in an input-data-unavailable setting. To achieve this, we propose a two-part approach where a rain creation network and a rain removal network work in conjunction, each trying to influence the other for accurate data translation. A high-level rain information information is then extracted by inferring the rain removal network and used to control the rain creation network. Experimental outcomes on two public data sets prove the effectiveness of our method, resulting in realistic rain effects across various scenes. A physical experiment further validates the proposed information's controllability over rain intensity.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their adoption is hindered by the time and expense of these comparisons, especially when dealing with large state-action spaces and frequent comparisons needed for clustering-based methods. This research proposes enhancing the efficiency of cluster ranking by incorporating visual aids. The strategy involves grouping states into clusters, presenting each as a video segment, and soliciting human comparisons to determine preferred clusters. These efficient human comparisons can then be utilized to train reinforcement learning models that deliver optimal rewards. We assessed the proposed approach's performance in comparative evaluations and preferred reward prediction accuracy across multiple setups, revealing substantial improvements in efficiency and predictive accuracy, respectively, compared to existing methodologies.

The continuum problem has been shown to be independent of ZFC through various proofs, revealing a common theme in these proofs - an abstract model theory element. This suggests an essential link between the possibility of continuous model functions and the continuum's independence, potentially offering insight into how model theory and set theory might be connected. This hypothesis suggests that model-theoretic properties, such as continuity, could serve as a basis for defining key set-theoretic concepts, like cardinality. Furthermore, it implies that certain model partnership theories, exploring the relationship between a model's possible functions and their properties, could offer a novel perspective on the continuum problem.

This study establishes conditions for bounded regions in n-dimensional Euclidean space to possess boundary Yamabe constants greater than zero. Specifically, we prove that for standard balls, this condition is both necessary and sufficient. We also derive an inequality that holds for all bounded domains in R^n with positive first eigenvalue for the Yamabe operator. Notably, this bound is the same as the first eigenvalue of the standard ball with an identical Dirichlet eigenvalue. The research further includes an upper bound with identical growth at infinity to the first eigenvalue with an additional parameter. A key step in this research involves an innovative application of a determinant identity. The research also provides an abstract framework, in which positive first eigenvalue becomes a constraint, to examine the long-term behavior of a nonlinear heat equation. Specifically, this involves estimating the decay rate of solutions and determining possible limits with decreasing norms.

Assessing drug consumption risk in the last decade has been commonly rated on a scale. A new approach proposes using the Five Factor Model of personality to assess the risk. This method involves a computerized test that evaluates the consumption risk based on five personality traits: Neuroticism, Extraversion, Openness to experience, Agreeableness, and Conscientiousness. The test's results can be visually displayed using a radar chart. Validity for this approach was examined in a study with 170 participants, comparing scores from the scale and the Five Factor Model. The results showed the approaches are equivalent in detecting high and low-risk consumers, but the Five Factor Model was found to be more accurate in assessing low-risk consumers. These findings suggest the validity of using the Five Factor Model of personality to assess drug consumption risk.

The prevalence of life-critical tasks still relies on traditional control systems, which utilize simplified rule sets, despite their drawbacks of inflexibility and difficulty in management. Recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence have shown that some advanced machine learning models can achieve exceptional accuracy, yet their interpretability remains a barrier, preventing their direct use in applications requiring transparency. This paper introduces ATOMIC, a novel approach that leverages automated machine learning models within an expert system framework, which utilizes human-editable rule sets that guide the choice of models, their input pre-processing, post-processing, and parameter settings, as well as logical sequencing, for each decision point, enabling the creation of intelligent systems capable of leveraging the power of modern machine learning models in a transparent and customizable manner. Three case studies showcasing the effectiveness of ATOMIC in real-world applications are presented, and an in-depth exploration of the design of ATOMIC, its modular architecture, and its extensibility in future versions are presented.

A key challenge in the financial sector is optimizing portfolios, a problem exacerbated by uncertainty that significantly impacts investors' decision-making processes and leads to market inefficiencies. Researchers have developed the HHL algorithm to optimize portfolios using quantum techniques, leveraging its exponential speedup in solving linear systems of equations. Nonetheless, implementing HHL in its full glory proves impractical for current Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum computers due to stringent requirements. In response to this limitation, researchers proposed a modified version of the HHL algorithm, which forgoes the need for precise phase estimation and enables the creation of portfolios optimized under noisy conditions. This novel version of the HHL algorithm was tested with real hardware and simulated environments, where it was found to outperform classical optimization algorithms in terms of return, particularly in scenarios mimicking market losses.

To enhance data efficiency of modern large-scale multimodal training and facilitate better integration of text and audio by sync points, a novel loss function called speech-text based bidirectional focus (STBF) is proposed for the joint training of speech and audio models. A key advantage of STBF is its capability to leverage the extensive available text data for model pretraining, modifying the traditional multi-modal framework to prioritize the alignment of corresponding text and audio segments. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating the STBF loss yields significant improvements in speech recognition accuracy, particularly when performing fine-tuning on limited labeled data. Furthermore, it is shown that pretraining an encoder using the STBF loss and training the remaining components separately leads to substantial gains in accuracy compared to a baseline approach.

Fixed cross-section averages within specific intervals for the total cross-section in proton-proton collisions have been computed and examined in detail across a range of mid to high energies. To identify similar patterns, the analysis is extended to proton-neutron, antiproton-antiproton, and several other combination collisions involving protons, antiprotons, or neutrons. Notably, some calculations also include data from the Large Hadron Collider. A mathematical model is proposed to explain these findings, effectively utilizing available experimental evidence. However, the current data is still somewhat limited, particularly in the lower energy range, where more comprehensive measurements would be beneficial. Additionally, the model predicts the behavior of total cross-sections in proton-ant neutron collisions, expanding the existing dataset to include more experimental validation.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a randomly generated uniform parking distribution of size $n$, denoted as $\pi_n$. We establish that the expected first position in $\pi_n$, denoted as $E[I_{n,1}]$, follows the recurrence relation $\frac{n-1}{n}\cdot E[I_{n-1,1}]+1$ and grows according to the rate of $n^{1/3}$. Furthermore, we show that the normalized first position, when normalized by $n^{1/3}$, converges to the distribution of the first component of the zigzag Poisson traitor finding scheme, which is derived from independent, uniformly distributed sequences. We further demonstrate that the normalized parking Meir-Moon numbers follow the same distribution. This work builds on previous research on random parking distributions and related combinatorial structures.

The research investigates the electrical behavior of superconducting nanowires, which have coherent quantum phase slip conduction, under the influence of an electric field applied across the grain boundaries. It is demonstrated that even a minimally applied voltage can inhibit this phenomenon and be inverted by increasing the applied electric field. A model based on the superconducting island's charge state manages to explain the observed characteristics, revealing the onset voltage to be directly related to the critical value of the coherent quantum current and exhibiting hysteresis in the switching process with delays matching those observed in measurements. Furthermore, the model predicts and our experiments confirm the involvement of photon participation in overcoming the barrier of quantum coherent energy. The system's dynamics are further mapped by varying the temperature and the critical current, demonstrating that the model provides an easily adjustable parameterization. It is concluded that nanowires exhibiting quantum phase slip noise are promising candidates for the creation of miniaturized, gate-controlled single electron transistors based on superconducting islands.

The T-dwarf planet GJ 229B, which orbits as a brown dwarf, is an important object of study due to its low mass and temperature that place it between the largest planets and brown dwarfs.  GJ 229B has the distinction of being the first known T-dwarf discovered, which made it an ideal target for research and has been observed with several telescopes in different wavelengths.  The application of the newly developed open-source spectral retrieval code APOLLO to available spectra for GJ 229B yielded the most precise chemical and physical properties to date, under the assumption of zero spin synchronization.
